subject: APAC dedicated pool provisioning for Nimbus - sizing & timeline
messages:
From: Emma Zhou <emma@nim-rb.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@nimbus.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: APAC dedicated pool + timeline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited about Redwood's predictable latency for inference. Procurement has asked me to get a firm ask over to you: we expect to go live with SAS-vision features in APAC in Q2, and need a dedicated capacity pool (single-tenant) located in Singapore (or nearest available APAC region) with predictable throughput for 10M token-minutes/month initially.

Highlights:
- Target go-live: May 1, 2026 (hard deadline)
- Initial capacity: enough to sustain 25 concurrent steady streams at 2048 token-length with 50ms p95 target where possible
- Model preference: mixture of H100 for peak workloads and A100 for background batch/rerank jobs
- Security: SOC2 evidence and basic IP protection (we can share the questionnaire separately)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can reserve a dedicated APAC pool and send an initial sizing + cost estimate this week? Procurement copied.

Best,
Emma Zhou
Head of AI Ops, Nimbus Robotics

---
Attachments: demand_curve_apac.png (png)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Emma Zhou <emma@nim-rb.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: APAC dedicated pool + timeline

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and deadline. We're confident we can support a Singapore-based dedicated pool; I want to loop in Marissa (capacity planning) and Karthik (deal routing/pricing).

Quick notes from my side:
- We can propose a mixed pool (H100 [preemptible options], A100) with a hot lane for low-latency inference and a warm lane for batch reranks.
- We'll need to validate local GPU availability for May 1 — there's a short supply window in late April for H100s.
- Can you confirm the expected peak tokens/minute distribution and whether you intend to run heavy offline batching overnight? That will materially affect reserved v. burst capacity sizing.

I'll ask Marissa to run a capacity calc and Karthik to outline pricing and contract implications. Expect an initial sizing spreadsheet by Thursday.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: APAC dedicated pool + timeline (capacity calc attached)

Jonas / Karthik — attaching an initial capacity model (capacity_calc_2026.xlsx) and a quick demand curve export (demand_curve_apac.png). High-level takeaways:

- Baseline reservation: 8 x H100 equivalent nodes + 12 x A100 nodes gives us ~30 concurrent steady low-latency streams at 2048 tokens with room for 2x burst for short windows.
- If Nimbus plans heavy overnight batch (>=40% of monthly tokens), we can rely on cheaper A100 batch lanes and use H100 for live traffic — that reduces committed H100 by ~25%.
- Lead time risk: H100 procurement in APAC is tight for late April; recommended path:
  1) Commit to a short MOU to reserve H100s (30-day hold)
  2) Begin canary with A100-only runs in early April to validate prompts and KV cache patterns
  3) Ramp H100 activation once hardware is confirmed

I'll mark cost impacts in the spreadsheet (spreadsheet tab: "Commit vs Burst") and include a suggested tranche schedule to align with Nimbus's contract milestones.

Attachments: capacity_calc_2026.xlsx (xlsx), demand_curve_apac.png (png)

- Marissa
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emma Zhou <emma@nim-rb.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: APAC dedicated pool provisioning for Nimbus - sizing & timeline

Emma / team — thanks for the patience. Per Marissa's calc, here's the preliminary commercial plan:

- Proposal: 12-month reserved commitment (tranche-based) covering the initial H100/A100 mix with a 60/40 split of reserved compute hours (reduces unit cost by ~18% vs on-demand).
- Upfront: we suggest a two-step activation: a small initial commit to secure H100 hold (MOU) + a larger reserved purchase once canary completes.
- SLA: 99.5% uptime SLA for the dedicated pool with documented fallback to on-hosted models in rare capacity degradation events.
- Contract timeline: we can have a draft MOU and SOW in 5 business days; procurement can use the attached MOU template.

Next actions: Jonas, can you confirm Nimbus's legal lead for contracting? Emma / procurement, happy to jump on a short call to walk procurement through the MOU and tranche plan.

Karthik
Head of Strategic Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Karthik / Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement confirms they can proceed with the MOU route to secure H100 hold. Legal is Mina Patel (mina.patel@nimbus.com) — copied procurement for intros.

A couple of clarifications before we lock dates:
- Can Redwood guarantee H100 activation by April 25 if we sign the MOU by Feb 24? We need the H100s online for an integration window in early May.
- For the SLA fallback, will the on-hosted model fallback preserve token privacy? We need confirmation that PII is not shared with other tenants during fallback windows.

If you can send a short note answering those two items and the final tranche numbers we can escalate to our CFO for approval. Happy to book a 30-min sync Friday if that helps.

Best,
Emma
Head of AI Ops, Nimbus Robotics
